Attendance and participation at the City of La Verne Planning Commission meetings are welcomed and
appreciated. Community engagement provides the Planning Commission with valuable information. Regular

Meetings are held on the 2 Wednesday of every month. In compliance with the American Disabilities Act,
any person with a disability who requires a modification or accommodation in order to participate in a
meeting should contact the City Clerk’s Office at (909) 596-8726 at least 48 hours prior to the meeting.

The Council Chambers will be open to the public at 6:00 p.m. In an effort keep a safe environment and to
minimize the spread of the COVID-19 Virus, the City will be limiting occupancy and requiring masking for all
that will be in attendance. Materials related to an item on this agenda, submitted to the Planning
Commission after distribution of the agenda packet, are available for public inspection at the meeting or in
the Community Development Department during normal business hours.

At its meeting of September 8, 2021, the Planning Commission continued the public hearing to a
future date in order to allow an “in-person” meeting for resident participation. Further, the
Planning Commission limited the future meeting’s discussion of the project to traffic and
transportation issues related to the Fruit Street project.

Based on the Planning Commission comments, staff has prepared a draft letter from the Planning
Commission to the City Council strongly recommending that the Council prioritize the full
funding and installation of a traffic signal at the intersection of Fruit and Amherst Streets.

The draft letter to the City Council is attached to this memo. The full agenda report and all
attachments can be found on the City’s website under the September 8, 2021, agenda packet.

Staff recommends that the Planning Commission re-open the continued public hearing in order to
discuss traffic and transportation as it pertains to the project. Staff will be available to answer
Commissioner questions after public comments.
   CITY OF LA VERNE
  PLANNING COMMISSION

September 28, 2021

Honorable Mayor and City Council Members
City of La Verne
3660 D Street
La Verne, CA 91750

RE: Brandywine’s Fruit Street Residential Project

Dear Mayor Hepburn and Council Members:

On behalf of the La Verne Planning Commission, I am writing you to formally encourage you to
prioritize the funding and construction/installation of a traffic signal at the intersection of Fruit Street
and Amherst Street, as shown to meet the warrants with the traffic analysis that was conducted for the
proposed residential development at 3717 Fruit Street.

The Planning Commission has discussed this project, and has heard the concerns of the residents, and
feel that this signal should be a priority for the City and should be added to the City’s Capital
Improvement Plan, ideally so that the signal could be installed and in operation once the project is
completed.

We understand that this is ultimately the City Council’s decision, but we wished to formally inform
you that we feel this is important to prioritize.

Please feel free to contact me or any other members of the Planning Commission should you wish to
discuss further.

Sincerely,

Jason Simison
Planning Commission Chair

CITY OF LA VERNE

  MINUTES OF THE SPECIAL MEETING
  Tuesday, September 28, 2021

1.  Chairperson Simison called the regular meeting of the La Verne Planning
  Commission to order at 6:30 p.m.

2.  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  Commissioner Allison led the Pledge of Allegiance.

3.  ROLL CALL: Planning Commissioners present: Thomas Allison, Jason
  Simison, and Jeff Allred. Absent: Jason Lorge. Advisory personnel present:
  Community Development Director Eric Scherer, City Attorney Bob Kress, City
  Engineer Cody Howing, Contract Planner Vanessa Norwood and Secretary
  Natalie Hiatt.

4.  PUBLIC COMMENT

  Chairperson Simison opened public comment. One public comment was received
  by Danita Beauchamp but it was sent in error.

  Chairperson Simison stated that the Public Hearing will focus on traffic. Public
  comment was closed.

  Mr. Scherer stated that the September 8th virtual meeting was continued to an in-
  person meeting. Since the last meeting the applicant tried to make contact with
  Cynthia Gabaldon but was not successful. Staff drafted a recommendation letter
  to City Council addressing the traffic concerns (attached). The letter can still be
  modified by the Commission.

  Mr. Scherer recommended continuing public hearing.

  Chairperson Simison asked for public comment. He reminded those present that
  masks are required under the current order and comments will be limited to 3
  minutes for each speaker.

  There were 9 public comments received via email or letters.

  2
 Planning Commission Minutes
September 28, 2021
  The following speakers spoke in opposition to the project:
  Danita Beauchamp
  Lily Brainard
  Cynthia Gabaldon
  Joe Gabaldon

  The following speakers spoke in support of the project:
  Alex Hernandez
  Brian Bowcock
  Kathy Kalousek

  Chairperson Simison closed public hearing.

  The Commissioners asked questions regarding the placement of a new traffic
  signal, the driveway location, and the traffic study. Mr. Howing and Mr. Scherer
  addressed the speakers concerns.

  The Commissioners recognized the significance of the traffic issues and the
  residents’ concerns but also recognized the quality of the proposed development.

  It was moved by Commissioner Allison and seconded by Commissioner Allred to
  recommend approval to the City Council. A letter will be sent to Council
  addressing the Commissioners’ recommendations for the Fruit Street project.
  Motion carried by a 3-0 vote.

ADJOURNMENT

  The meeting was adjourned at 7:53p.m. The next regular meeting of the Planning
  Commission will be held October 13, 2021 at 6:30 p.m. in the Council Chambers,
  3660 “D” Street, La Verne, CA 91750.
